EXPERIMENT DESIGN DOCUMENT — v1.0 (FINAL)
Comparing JaxMARL PPO vs Q-Learning on SMAX: wall-clock training time and normalized score

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
STATUS AND SCOPE
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
• THIS IS A DESIGN ONLY. No experiment has been run. No training, no evaluation, and no results are claimed anywhere in this document. All numbers are planning estimates.
• Design-only task per brief: repositories and compute are not required for this deliverable. Because the execution compute budget is unstated, Section 8 provides an explicit feasibility/budget analysis with scaling tiers rather than assuming resources.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
1. RESEARCH QUESTION AND HYPOTHESES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Q: How does JaxMARL's PPO compare to Q-Learning in SMAX environments in terms of training time and normalized score?
• H1 (score): On small/medium maps, both algorithms reach comparable normalized scores within the fixed budget; on the hard asymmetric map, QMIX is expected to retain an advantage (expected value-decomposition benefits), while on very large maps PPO may degrade more slowly.
• H2 (time): JaxMARL's vectorized JAX implementation makes both algorithms fast; wall-clock time-to-budget is hypothesized to scale sub-linearly with map size for both, with the gap between algorithms narrowing as map size grows (both dominated by env stepping).
Both hypotheses are stated for the record; the design is descriptive/comparative, not confirmatory of a mechanism.

INTERPRETATION ASSUMPTION (PROMINENT, per resolution 1): The task says "Q-Learning" without pinning a variant. JaxMARL ships value-decomposition Q-learning baselines, not a plain (non-decomposed) multi-agent Q-learning baseline. This design adopts QMIX as the primary Q-Learning representative, with VDN as an optional secondary arm if budget allows (Section 8, Tier 2). No claim is made about which variant the task author intended; all conclusions are explicitly conditioned on this interpretation.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
2. ENVIRONMENTS (SMAX MAPS)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Six maps spanning scale and one hard asymmetric case (map names per documented JaxMARL SMAX suite; to be verified against the pinned repo version before execution — see Section 9):

  Tier / Map            Allies vs Enemies   Rationale
  Small  / 5m_vs_6m      5 vs 6             canonical easy map, fast runs
  Small  / 2s3z          2 stalkers+3 zealots small mixed unit types
  Medium / 3s5z          3 vs 5             standard medium benchmark
  Medium / 6h_vs_8z      6 vs 8             hard asymmetric case
  Large  / 10m_vs_11m    10 vs 11           large-marine scale test
  Large  / 2c64_40z      64 vs 40           extreme scale; JAX speedup claims strongest here; first candidate to drop if over budget

Environment settings: JaxMARL default SMAX configuration (including the defaults documented in the JaxMARL paper, e.g., move-state/local-obs feature flags) for both algorithms; identical env config for both arms. Stochastic env steps ON. Env config YAMLs are pinned and archived alongside results.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
3. ALGORITHMS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
• PPO arm: JaxMARL IPPO baseline (baselines/IPPO/main.py), shipped per-map Hydra configs.
• Q-Learning arm (primary): JaxMARL QMIX baseline (baselines/QMIX/main.py), shipped per-map configs. Optional secondary: VDN (same codebase, config switch).
• Hyperparameters: DEFAULTS ONLY from the pinned JaxMARL version's per-map configs. No retuning. This is a deliberate fairness/feasibility trade-off (see Threats T3).
• Version pinning: exact git commit hash of JaxMARL, plus versions of jax/jaxlib and CUDA, recorded in the run manifest. The repo is cloned once; a checksum of the tree is recorded.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
4. INDEPENDENT / DEPENDENT VARIABLES AND CONTROLS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
• IV: algorithm ∈ {IPPO, QMIX} (+ optional VDN); Moderator: map (6 levels); nuisance: seed (5–10 levels).
• DV1 (primary time): wall-clock seconds to reach the fixed per-map env-timestep budget (Table in §6), JIT warm-up excluded from the primary figure but reported separately per run.
• DV2 (secondary time): time-normalized AUC of normalized score vs. wall-clock hours, sampled at eval checkpoints.
• DV3 (score): anchor-based normalized score at the budget (definition in §5), plus learning curves of normalized score vs. env steps and vs. wall-clock.
• Controls: same device, sequential runs (never concurrent), same eval protocol both arms, same env config, same commit, warm-up run per (algo, map) pair before timed runs, timestamps and device telemetry logged.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
5. METRIC DEFINITIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Score metric: WIN RATE (assumption; see §10 A6). Justification: SMAX inherits SMAC's win/loss episode outcome ("all enemies defeated" without timeout), win rate is the standard SMAC/SMAC-style benchmark metric, is bounded and comparable across maps, and is less sensitive to return-scale differences between algorithms than raw episode return. Raw episode return is logged but reported only as a sanity check, not as the primary score.

Normalized score (per map m, per run, at a given checkpoint):
  NS = clip( (WR − WR_random) / (WR_heuristic − WR_random), 0, 1 )
where WR_random is the win rate of an untrained/random policy evaluated in the same harness (20+ episodes, same eval protocol), and WR_heuristic is the win rate of SMAX's built-in scripted/heuristic agent (e.g., "independent" attack-closest policy) under the same protocol.
  Fallback: if a heuristic anchor is unavailable or degenerate (WR_heuristic − WR_random < 0.05) for a map, use min–max normalization over the pooled observed range of both algorithms on that map, and flag the map's NS values as fallback-based in all figures.

Training-time accounting:
  • Timed region: from the first post-compile training step to the step at which the cumulative env-timestep budget is reached, measured with explicit device synchronization.
  • JIT warm-up (compilation) time recorded separately per (algo, map); excluded from the primary metric because it is a one-off, not per-sample cost; also reported as time-to-budget-inclusive-of-compile for transparency.
  • Eval time is excluded from training time (it is protocol overhead, identical across arms) but logged.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
6. RUN MATRIX AND ESTIMATED COSTS (ESTIMATES ONLY — nothing run)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Per-map env-timestep budgets and per-run wall-clock estimates (single modern data-center GPU, e.g., A100-class; ranges wide because they are pre-execution guesses derived from JaxMARL's reported throughput, NOT measurements):

  Map          Budget (env steps)  Est. h/run (IPPO)  Est. h/run (QMIX)
  5m_vs_6m     1M                  0.3–0.6            0.3–0.6
  2s3z         2M                  0.5–0.9            0.5–0.9
  3s5z         3M                  0.9–1.6            0.9–1.6
  6h_vs_8z     3M                  1.0–1.8            1.0–1.8
  10m_vs_11m   5M                  1.5–2.5            1.5–2.5
  2c64_40z     5M                  3.0–6.0            3.0–6.0

Run matrix (primary design): 2 algorithms × 6 maps × 5 seeds = 60 runs.
Estimated totals (5 seeds, per map, both algorithms = 10 runs × est. h/run):
  5m_vs_6m ≈ 3–6 h; 2s3z ≈ 5–9 h; 3s5z ≈ 9–16 h; 6h_vs_8z ≈ 10–18 h; 10m_vs_11m ≈ 15–25 h; 2c64_40z ≈ 30–60 h.
  TOTAL ≈ 72–134 GPU-hours (~3–6 days of continuous single-GPU time), plus ~5–15 min compile warm-up per (algo, map) pair (12 pairs ≈ 1–3 h total) and eval overhead (~10–15% of training time).

Budget tiers (feasibility analysis, since the GPU-hour budget is unstated):
  Tier 1 (full, ~72–134 GPU-h): all 6 maps, 5 seeds. Preferred.
  Tier 1+ (~145–270 GPU-h): 10 seeds instead of 5.
  Tier 2 (+40–120 GPU-h): adds VDN as the secondary Q-Learning arm (same matrix), answering the interpretation ambiguity empirically.
  Tier 3 (degraded, ~45–75 GPU-h): drop 2c64_40z (−30–60 h); 5 maps × 5 seeds.
  Tier 4 (minimal, ~35–55 GPU-h): drop 2c64_40z AND shorten large-map budgets 10m_vs_11m 5M→3M (−6–10 h); 5 maps, reduced budgets, 5 seeds.
  CPU-only fallback caveat: JAX's headline speedups (and JaxMARL's claims) are GPU-dependent; on CPU the wall-clock comparison loses external validity and total cost explodes (likely 10× or worse). CPU-only execution is NOT recommended; if forced, report it as a distinct, non-comparable condition and restrict conclusions accordingly.
  Decision rule: if the budget allows < Tier 3, reduce seeds to 3 on the two largest maps first (flagged as low-power), rather than dropping the hard map.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
7. EVALUATION PROTOCOL (EXACT)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
• Cadence: evaluation every 50,000 env steps of training (20 checkpoints at 1M, 100 at 5M; final eval always at the exact budget).
  Cadence is expressed in env steps (not wall-clock) so both arms get identical checkpoint alignment; the time-normalized AUC interpolates between checkpoints.
• Per checkpoint: 32 evaluation episodes, greedy policy, deterministic eval env seeding (fixed eval-seed base per checkpoint, shared across algorithms and seeds), on the same device type as training.
• Anchors (random policy, heuristic baseline) evaluated once per map with 100 episodes each, same protocol, before the run campaign.
• Recorded per checkpoint: win rate, mean/std episode return, episode length, wall-clock timestamp, cumulative env steps.
• Win rate is the primary score (§5); return logged for sanity checks only.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
8. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS PLAN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
• Per-map comparisons (5 seeds/arm):
  – Score: final NS at budget; mean ± 95% bootstrap CI (10,000 resamples over seeds); Welch's t-test or Mann–Whitney depending on normality, with Holm correction across the 6 maps.
  – Time: wall-clock to budget; mean ± 95% CI; report the ratio IPPO/QMIX with CI (ratio is more interpretable than the difference).
  – Time-to-threshold: first checkpoint where NS ≥ 0.8 of the heuristic anchor (or final NS if never reached); compared per map.
  – Time-normalized AUC: computed by trapezoidal integration of NS vs. wall-clock hours; CI via seed-level bootstrap.
• Aggregate: rliable-style IQM of NS across maps with stratified bootstrap (2,000 iterations); performance-profile and probability-of-improvement curves over wall-clock. LIMITATION (explicit): with only 6 maps, the aggregate is a descriptive summary of these maps, not a population-level inference over all SMAX tasks; per-map results carry equal weight in the narrative.
• Effect sizes reported (Cohen's d or rank-biserial) alongside p-values; no dichotomous "significant/not" framing in the conclusions.
• Pre-registration: run matrix, budgets, metric definitions, and analysis plan (this document) are fixed before any run; deviations logged.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
9. THREATS TO VALIDITY
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
T1 — Unverified repository details. The design workspace contained no JaxMARL source (only task.json; network disabled; jax/jaxmarl not importable). Map names, baseline entry points (baselines/IPPO, baselines/QMIX), config flag names, and heuristic-baseline availability are from documented knowledge of the public repo and its paper and were NOT verified here. First execution step: clone the pinned version and validate every path/config name cited above; revise the design doc if any artifact differs.
T2 — Version drift. JaxMARL is actively developed; throughput and defaults change across versions. Mitigation: single pinned commit + dependency manifest; results stated as version-specific.
T3 — Hyperparameter-default confound. Defaults-only means each algorithm's tuning state is whatever the JaxMARL authors chose per map; a gap could reflect tuning effort, not algorithmic merit. Mitigation: document all hyperparameters per arm; sensitivity note in the report; retuning explicitly out of scope.
T4 — Hardware dependence of JAX speedup claims. Wall-clock conclusions are valid only for the declared GPU configuration; CPU-only execution would qualitatively change the comparison (see §8 Tier caveat). Concurrent runs on one device would distort timing; sequential-only is a design constraint, not a preference.
T5 — Q-Learning interpretation ambiguity. Results hold for QMIX (and optionally VDN), not for Q-learning in general; stated prominently in §1 and in every results summary.
T6 — Normalization anchors. Heuristic anchor quality varies per map; degenerate anchors trigger the min–max fallback, which makes cross-map aggregation slightly less comparable (mixed normalization bases are disclosed per map).
T7 — Compile-time treatment. Excluding JIT warm-up flatters both arms equally, but the relative share of compile time differs by map size; both figures (inclusive/exclusive) reported.
T8 — Seed variability at 5 seeds. CIs on 5 seeds are wide for hard maps where win rate is near 0 or 1; conclusions on such maps will be reported as inconclusive rather than forced. 10-seed tier preferred.
T9 — Budget truncation. Algorithms still improving at the budget get truncated NS values; learning-curve-at-budget is the primary score readout, and "time-to-threshold" analysis partially mitigates truncation bias.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
10. ASSUMPTIONS (proposed defaults, not task-fixed)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
A1. "Q-Learning" = QMIX (primary), VDN optional (resolution 1; prominent flag in §1).
A2. Fixed env-timestep budget is the primary time comparison; wall-clock AUC is secondary.
A3. SMAX heuristic agent provides a valid anchor on all maps (fallback defined).
A4. Defaults-only hyperparameters are acceptable (resolution 2).
A5. 5 seeds minimum, 10 preferred (resolution 2); estimates in §6 assume 5.
A6. Win rate (not raw return) is the normalized-score input, per §5 justification — flagged as an assumption per resolution 3(b).
A7. Sequential single-device execution (resolution 2).
A8. Timestep budgets per tier in §6 are design proposals; the researcher may set different budgets, and §6 estimates rescale linearly with budget.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
11. EXECUTION CHECKLIST (for the researcher, if/when approved to run)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
1. Clone JaxMARL at the chosen commit; verify all cited paths/configs (T1). 2. Smoke-test one run per arm on 5m_vs_6m to calibrate §6 estimates. 3. Evaluate random and heuristic anchors per map. 4. Warm-up runs per (algo, map) pair. 5. Execute the run matrix sequentially with logging (manifest: commit, config dump, seed, device, timestamps, compile time). 6. Analysis per §8. 7. Report with per-map tables, rliable aggregate, and the §9 threat disclosures.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
REMAINING UNCERTAINTIES (for the researcher)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
• Actual GPU model/availability at execution time (all §6 estimates are A100-class guesses).
• Whether VDN arm and 10-seed tier are affordable (drives Tier 1+ / Tier 2).
• Verified SMAX map list and heuristic-anchor availability in the pinned JaxMARL version (T1/T6) — must be checked at execution start.
• Final choice of timestep budgets (§6 proposals vs. task-author intent).

No experiment was run; all quantitative figures in this document are planning estimates or metric definitions, never results.

disclosed_researcher_facts.text: Evaluate and compare PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) and Q-Learning for multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) in the SMAX (StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge in JAX) environment, focusing on training efficiency and performance.
JaxMARL, a JAX-based MARL library that enables large-scale parallelization and efficient GPU-accelerated training.
- SMAX: A JAX-based reimplementation of the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge (SMAC), designed for multi-agent micromanagement tasks.
